tips.title: Perimeter shadow-line LED cove
tips.spark: How do you build the soft glow around this ceiling?

economy.specification: Surface-mounted 45° aluminium LED channel with an opal diffuser, a 24 V / 2700 K strip (10 W/m) and a plug-in driver.
economy.detail: Fix the slim channel directly at the ceiling–wall junction. Route the low-voltage supply to an accessible plug-in driver.
economy.difference: A visible surface profile replaces the recessed cove, reducing ceiling construction work.

standard.specification: A 50 mm dropped plasterboard ceiling with an aluminium shadow-gap cove profile, 24 V / 2700 K COB LED strip (14.4 W/m) and a remote driver.
standard.detail: Prepare a flat ceiling, then frame a perimeter pocket set back 50–80 mm from the walls. Fit the LED extrusion and diffuser into the trough, run 24 V wiring to an accessible driver, and finish the plasterboard edge to the trim bead.
standard.difference: A recessed profile conceals the light source and creates the continuous ceiling glow.

premium.specification: Trimless plaster-in cove with an indirect-light baffle, dual-circuit 2200–3000 K tunable-white ribbon (CRI 95+) and DALI-2 or Casambi drivers.
premium.detail: Integrate the architectural profile into the ceiling finish. Coordinate the baffle, two lighting circuits and compatible dimming controls before closing the ceiling; retain driver access.
premium.difference: The profile disappears into the finish, with adjustable white tone and more lighting control.

tips.check: Calculate the measured run × W/m: for example, 4 m × 14.4 W/m = 57.6 W before the driver manufacturer’s reserve. Check cable voltage drop, dimmer compatibility and driver access.

quick.standard: Recessed cove · 24 V COB · 2700 K · 14.4 W/m
quick.premium: Trimless cove · CRI 95+ · 2200–3000 K · coordinated DALI-2 / Casambi control

tips.title: Timber slat feature wall
tips.spark: What is behind the oak slats — and how are they fixed?

economy.specification: Ready-made foil-wrapped MDF acoustic slat panels, 2400 × 600 mm, fixed to a prepared flat wall.
economy.detail: Prepare and flatten the wall, then install the panels with the specified high-grab polyurethane adhesive and finishing pins. Plan cable openings before fixing the panels.
economy.difference: Oak-effect foil and direct fixing replace natural veneer and the battened substructure.

standard.specification: White-oak-veneered MDF slats on a 9 mm recycled PET acoustic felt backer, fixed to timber counter-battens with black fasteners.
standard.detail: Remove the wallpaper and prepare the substrate. Fix 20 × 45 mm counter-battens at 400 mm centres to suitable wall structure; fasten through the felt gaps. Form electrical and AV openings behind the TV before completing the cladding.
standard.difference: Natural oak veneer adds real timber texture; the battened build-up provides space to coordinate fixings and cabling.

premium.specification: Custom solid white oak battens, 25 × 35 mm, on hidden rear clips over acoustic fabric, with clear UV-matt polyurethane lacquer and integrated cable chases.
premium.detail: Detail the batten spacing and hidden clips as a custom assembly. Coordinate the acoustic backing, concealed cabling and finish before installation.
premium.difference: Solid oak and concealed fixings replace the prefabricated veneer panels.

tips.check: Acoustic performance belongs to a tested panel, cavity and backing assembly—not the slat appearance alone. Check reaction-to-fire requirements, wall fixing and ventilation around AV equipment.

quick.economy: 2400 × 600 mm foil-faced panels · prepared flat wall
quick.standard: Oak veneer · 9 mm PET backer · 20 × 45 mm battens
quick.premium: 25 × 35 mm solid-oak battens · hidden clips · coordinated cable chases

tips.title: Recessed curtain pocket and track
tips.spark: How do the curtains meet the ceiling without a visible rail?

economy.specification: A slim surface-mounted ceiling track screened by a 100 mm lightweight, primed MDF pelmet fascia.
economy.detail: Fix the track securely to suitable ceiling support, then fit and finish the pelmet to screen the mechanism from normal viewing height.
economy.difference: A surface pelmet hides the rail without forming a recess in the ceiling.

standard.specification: A plasterboard ceiling pocket, 150 mm wide × 100 mm deep, with a dual-channel aluminium curtain track fixed into structural framing.
standard.detail: Frame the pocket with UW/CW 50 steel profiles and 12.5 mm plasterboard. Finish the lower edge with a stop bead or aluminium trim; fix the continuous track into joists or timber noggings inside the recess.
standard.difference: The ceiling itself conceals the track, giving the full-height curtains a cleaner junction.

premium.specification: A flush plaster-in architectural curtain profile with a low-voltage motorised rail and an integrated indirect LED wash channel.
premium.detail: Coordinate the motor, low-voltage supply, lighting channel and ceiling profile before the ceiling is finished. Keep the rail and motor accessible for servicing.
premium.difference: Motorised operation and integrated lighting become part of a seamless ceiling detail.

tips.check: Size the pocket for the selected track, fabric fullness and stack-back. The 150 × 100 mm example is not a universal recess; check the window handle, radiator projection, support and motor access.

quick.economy: Surface track · 100 mm painted MDF pelmet
quick.standard: 150 × 100 mm example pocket · dual-channel track · structural fixing
quick.premium: Plaster-in profile · low-voltage motor · separate LED channel

tips.title: Floating shelves and low credenza
tips.spark: How are the floating shelves supported — and where do the TV cables go?

economy.specification: A modular laminate lowboard on a minimal plinth, paired with ready-made hollow-core floating shelves and standard concealed brackets.
economy.detail: Select shelf brackets and fixings for the wall and intended loads. Assemble the modular cabinet and plan simple cable routes before placing the TV equipment.
economy.difference: Stock modules and hollow-core shelves replace custom joinery and steel supports.

standard.specification: Custom oak-veneered plywood shelves with concealed steel support rods, plus a low credenza with Blum soft-close hardware on a recessed plinth.
standard.detail: Locate studs or sound masonry and add 45 × 95 mm timber noggings where required. Fix load-rated concealed brackets into structural support, slide on the shelves and secure from below. Route AV cables through grommets to the TV chase.
standard.difference: Fitted veneer joinery hides the supports and cabling while the recessed plinth lightens the cabinet’s appearance.

premium.specification: Bespoke rift-cut white oak millwork with an internal welded steel armature, warm-dim micro-LED shelf lighting and brush cable grommets.
premium.detail: Coordinate the structural armature, wall anchors and custom joinery as one assembly. Form the lighting routes and cable penetrations before the millwork is closed.
premium.difference: Solid timber, engineered hidden support and integrated lighting turn the storage into a complete fitted feature.

tips.check: Specify shelf span, depth and intended load before selecting concealed rods. Verify wall backing and bracket capacity as a complete assembly; retain cable bend space, equipment ventilation and driver access.

quick.economy: Stock lowboard · hollow-core shelves · verified concealed brackets
quick.standard: Oak-veneered plywood · concealed steel rods · soft-close hardware
quick.premium: Bespoke oak millwork · steel armature · replaceable shelf lighting

faqs: How do I get started?
Open the Briller studio, create an account and add a room photo or sketch. You can then add references and describe the direction you want to explore.
What knowledge is Briller built on?

Briller.House brings together Mike Briller’s personal experience and the practical know-how of his colleagues — architects, designers and construction workers — in an AI-assisted knowledge base of modern design and construction solutions. Mike is the face of this shared expertise.
Will Briller preserve my room’s geometry?

Briller is designed to use the existing walls, doors and windows as constraints. Check each generated image against your original room; AI results are visual concepts, not construction drawings or a guarantee of exact geometry.
What can I upload?
The workflow accepts room photos or sketches, style references and optional architectural drawings. Check the studio upload interface for current supported file types and size limits.
Can I talk to Briller in Ukrainian?
Yes. Briller supports natural-language interaction, including English and Ukrainian, with text and voice input.
What is included in the Free plan?
Up to 3 active projects, 20 iterations per month, a Designed with Briller watermark and basic assistant suggestions.
How do credits and top-ups work?

Paid plans include a monthly credit allowance. Additional credit packs do not expire. Operation costs, renewal timing and any subscription-credit rollover rules should be checked in the app before purchase.
Where do I pay or manage my subscription?

Billing takes place in the Briller app through Stripe. Subscription management is available through the Stripe Customer Portal in your account. Check the portal for cancellation options and the effective end date.
Can I use a render commercially?
All paid plans — Explorer, Pro Design and Studio / Architect — include commercial licensing. Review the current app terms for the scope of your licence.
Are my projects public?

The website inspiration gallery contains curated reference photography. It does not read or publish private app projects. The app’s data retention, sharing and AI-processing policies must be confirmed in its final Privacy Policy.
Are Briller’s suggestions construction advice?
Use them as design ideas to discuss with qualified professionals. Verify measurements, structural changes, lighting, electrical work and material installation before implementation.
How can I contact support?
Email hello@briller.house with your question. Avoid including passwords, payment details or sensitive project information.
